motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The house ease for every CSS transition.

motion.name: scroll-hour
motion.value: p: holds on each whole hour while that scene's text is fully on screen; linear between holds; gaps at least 120px
motion.purpose: The single driver of all time-bound motion, exposed as --p.

motion.name: smoothstep
motion.purpose: Easing for scroll-bound motion: sky colour, sun path, screen wipe.

motion.name: screen-wipe
motion.value: incoming mask linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent edge%, #000 edge+6%) rising from the bottom over 30-70% of the gap; outgoing hidden once fully covered; no blur, no scale
motion.purpose: Phone screens changing hour (sticky desktop phone).

motion.name: clock-minute
motion.value: minute = lerp(hour time, next hour time, gap progress), rounded; digits swapped in place

motion.name: star-travel
motion.purpose: Time marker bound to the scroll.

motion.name: twinkle
motion.value: redraw at most every 60ms; runs only when stars show, viewport >= 900px, story in view, tab visible

motion.name: text-recolor
motion.purpose: Story text, caption and rail during the day/ink flip.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover and pressed state colour, background, lift.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: CSS durations collapse to 0.001ms; screens snap at the gap midpoint; clock holds each scene's time; stars do not twinkle; scrollIntoView uses auto

skyBodies.name: gradient
skyBodies.value: linear top 0, mid 0.55, low 1 of the interpolated key; colours eased with smoothstep(0.15, 0.85) inside each hour

skyBodies.name: sun
skyBodies.value: radius 3.4% of min(vw, vh); colour #ff9a4d to #ffd27a (morning), #fff7e6 (noon), back to #ff9a4d (dusk); halo radius 62% of min(vw, vh) in the key's glow; disc dims to 35% while crossing the morning copy band; gone by p 3.4

skyBodies.name: horizon-glow
skyBodies.value: radial from 50% 105%, radius 70% of max(vw, vh), key glow at 32% x glowA

skyBodies.name: moon
skyBodies.value: crescent, radius 3% of min(vw, vh), rgb(243,230,191) (gold-pale) cut by a 0.92r disc offset (+0.42r, -0.22r) with destination-out; halo gold-pale at 16%; rises in the gap from p 3.55 to 4.6

skyBodies.name: stars
skyBodies.value: 220 seeded, 0.6-1.5px, text-on-sky at 35-100%, twinkle 0.75 + 0.25 sin(t/900); visible before p 0.9 and after p 3.35

skyBodies.name: lattice
skyBodies.value: eight-point star tile, 132px cell, gold-light 0.8px stroke, 5% alpha, top 75% of the sky, from p 3.4

skyBodies.name: ridges
skyBodies.value: far at ~93% height (7% amplitude), near at ~98.5% (5%), the key's low colour darkened; fade toward mist when the sky is pale; far rim stroked 1.6px #ffc27a as the sun touches it

skyBodies.name: faint-mode
skyBodies.value: no measured gap (narrow layouts): sun and moon at 35% on a fixed path, rim light at 50%

narrative.overview:
The site is the Noorain app's world (mosque green, antique gold, warm paper, the eight-point star) carried onto the open web, with one addition the app does not have: the page ground is a sky. The landing page is a single day, and the sky is alive: a canvas drawn from the scroll position, its colours interpolating between six hour keys (dawn indigo into amber, misty morning green, pale midday mist, gold dusk, mosque-green night, late night). A sun climbs out from behind a low ridge, crosses the open gap between the copy and the phone, and sets on the far ridge with its rim lit; after dusk a crescent moon rises in the same gap, stars come out and twinkle, and the app's eight-point star lattice glows faintly over the night. Nothing is boxed on that sky. Headings, prose and the gold pill sit directly on it, and the only object is the near-black phone, which holds the app's real screens and lock-screen renderer and catches the light of the hour on its rim.

Density is low and the voice is calm: one heading, one paragraph and at most one action per hour, a 34rem text column, and a lot of sky. The story holds still while an hour's text is being read and moves only between hours: the clock runs minute by minute, the incoming screen wipes up over the outgoing one, and the rail star travels with the scroll. Type is the app's pairing, PT Serif for headings and Golos Text for everything else, with Amiri Quran reserved for scripture. Ornament is limited to the eight-point star and gold hairlines.

The legal pages are the Read mode of the same world: the app's green band (with the logo mark tiled faintly down its right edge) over a paper page, a 46rem column, and green as the selected state.
keyCharacteristics: The ground is the hour: a living, full-bleed sky drawn from the scroll position, never a flat dark hero.
The sun and moon keep to open sky: their path is measured from the layout, so they never pass behind the phone, the rail or the copy.
The story holds on each hour while its text is read, and moves only in the gaps between hours.
One object on the sky: the phone, sticky on desktop, inline under each hour on mobile; its rim takes the hour's light.
Gold is a hairline, a star, a time and one pill; green is a band and a selected state.
PT Serif headings at -0.02em, Golos Text body, Amiri Quran only for the Quran.
The eight-point star is the only ornament: the rail marker, and at night a faint lattice in the sky.

rules.name: The Sky Is the Surface Rule
rules.body: The landing page's ground is the living sky, full-bleed and fixed behind the story. No card, panel or section fill sits on it; the FAQ and footer return to flat night only after the day has ended.

rules.name: The Open Sky Rule
rules.body: The sun and moon travel only through sky that is empty: their path is computed from the measured gap between the copy and the phone, and where no gap exists (phones, narrow screens) they are drawn at 35% so text over them stays legible.

rules.name: The One Gold Fill Rule
rules.body: Gold fills exactly three things on a dark ground: the Telegram pill, the selected language segment and the skip link. Every other gold is a hairline, a star, a time or text. This deliberately relaxes the app's Gold Is a Line Rule for the site's single call to action.

rules.name: The Gold Keeps Its Contrast Rule
rules.body: On dark grounds gold text is gold-light; on paper or a pale sky it is gold-ink. Never antique gold as text on a light ground.

rules.name: The Luminance Flip Rule
rules.body: When the relative luminance of the sky's mid colour passes 0.19 (the WCAG crossover where dark text out-contrasts light), the page enters day: story text switches to day-ink and day-muted, rail times to ink at 72% with the active one in gold-ink, and the phone's drop turns green-tinted with a paper-white rim and glow. Below 0.19 it flips back. The flip is computed, never tied to a scene.

rules.name: The Untouched Scripture Rule
rules.body: Arabic is set only in Amiri Quran at weight 400: never bold, never letter-spaced, never truncated, never overlaid with ornament. A soft text shadow is allowed only where it sits on a wallpaper.

rules.name: The Subtitle-Below Rule
rules.body: A heading may be followed by a lede or note; nothing is set above it. No eyebrows or kickers.

rules.name: The Real Clock Rule
rules.body: Times on the phone change like a real clock: whole minutes, digits swapped in place, no roll or slide.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: The phone is the only thing on the page with physical depth. Text and controls stay flat on the sky.

rules.name: The Hour's Light Rule
rules.body: The phone's rim and side glow are lit by the sky, never by a fixed colour: they read `--sky-glow` and `--sky-glow-a`, which the scroll loop sets from the current hour's glow key.

dos: **Do** let the hour's sky be the page ground and set text directly on it.
**Do** derive every time-bound thing (sky, clock, screens, rail and strip stars) from the one scroll value p, and hold it still while an hour's text is being read.
**Do** keep the sun and moon in measured open sky, and draw them at 35% wherever text may cross them.
**Do** flip text to day-ink by the sky's computed luminance (0.19), not by which scene is showing.
**Do** keep the phone the only raised object, light its rim from `--sky-glow`, and show real app screens or the app's own renderer inside it.
**Do** use gold-light for gold on dark and gold-ink for gold on paper or a pale sky.
**Do** make every control a full pill and every ornament the eight-point star.
**Do** keep one action per hour at most: the gold Telegram pill, optionally with one gold text link.
**Do** set Arabic only in Amiri Quran at line-height 2, right-aligned, unbolded and untracked.

**Do** use the house ease (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for CSS transitions and smoothstep for scroll-bound motion, and let `prefers-reduced-motion` snap screens, hold the clock and still the stars.
**Do** keep tap targets at least 40px (34px for language segments) and body text at 17px.
donts: **Don't** put cards, panels or a feature grid on the sky.
**Don't** blur or scale a phone screen while its hour's text is on screen; screens change only in the gaps.
**Don't** fill anything else with gold beyond the Telegram pill, the selected language and the skip link.
**Don't** place eyebrows or kickers above headings.
**Don't** add ornament beyond the eight-point star and the logo mark, or any imagery of living beings. The sky's own bodies (sun, moon, stars, ridges) are the ground, not ornament.
**Don't** decorate, crop, bold, track or overlay ornament on Quran text.
**Don't** use emoji or text glyphs as icons; icons are inline SVG at 1.25em.
